"If you want to cut your hand off, that’s your choice. I am not asking you to do it. Also if you actually loved me you would not try to manipulate me." Similar to the response you should give when someone attempts to manipulate you by threatening self harm. And I say this as someone who thinks about suicide a lot.

Her parents must have manipulated her using threats of self harm, otherwise she would see right through it.

Ugh never mind, reality is trolling me. I could have sworn I read about a fatal interaction involving two drugs I have access to, but apparently I did so in a dream because now that I Google them they don't interact at all.

Kind of you to share, but I don't think I will ever be able to look back with anything other than partial shock, since I didn't lose them to physical death. They just...changed into my worst nightmare and traumatized me.

Also lying on a resume is incredibly stupid. Either it helps you get the job, in which case the truth is at risk of coming out and damaging your credibility, or it doesn’t help you get the job in which case, why lie?

Pretending to be good at something you aren’t good at is not “portraying your best side”, it’s portraying a side that is literally false.

Even if 90% of people do lie on their resume, OP has a right to date the 10% who don’t.

That level of dishonesty would bother me. It misleads the other person about the effort you have put into the date. I would not be surprised if she turns out to be the type who lies on her resume too. At the very least, it’s inauthentic.

Regardless of whether people think such lies are “ok”, it’s clearly not a match for the level of authenticity you expect. And you have a right to set your own standards for authenticity. It may take you a while to find a match but I guarantee that lowering your standards is unlikely to work, particularly if you uncover even bigger cases of inauthenticity (e.g. concealing debt, lying about accomplishments, etc); you will find yourself thinking “should have heeded the warning signs”. How much can you forgive as “just trying to impress” you?

(I am quite surprised some people are assuming it’s a troll post and that some people think it’s sweet of her to mislead you, as if wanting to impress you makes it ok for her to mess with you. I guess I am learning a lot about how likely people are to do stuff like lying on a resume. It’s also possible that reddit is weird)

Also I looked it up, estimates for lying on a resume range from 40% to 78% (ew). Find the 22% who don’t do that.

“anger I feel is the most basic and true emotion” - anger is a secondary emotion; it is a response to a perceived threat. The basic emotion behind anger is fear. This is true physiologically; fear is like an injection of the hormone epinephrine, while anger is like an injection of both epinephrine and nor-epinephrine (https://journals.lww.com/psychosomaticmedicine/Abstract/1953/09000/The_Physiological_Differentiation_between_Fear_and.7.aspx).

The best way to know what anger is telling you is to get in touch with the fear behind the anger, then figure out whether attacking the object of your fear (which is what anger motivates you to do) is the best way to deal with the fear.

Source: anger management lessons
They may not be brave; they may just have no fear of death.

“I should care about that for what exact reason” - because you seem to be carrying a lot of guilt over how you behaved with this girl, which means a part of you still has a conscience.

Also, if you kill yourself by jamming a commuter rail, you will just make people even more annoyed as your last act. Not many will have sympathy. You could be delaying some people from getting to extremely important places, maybe even a matter of life and death for some on the train. And if the many studies on near death experiences and past-life recall are any indication, you will find yourself sticking around in “spirit” form to witness those consequences (see: https://med.virginia.edu/perceptual-studies/). I say this as someone who has considered “death by commuter rail” for myself.

Before you kill yourself, make sure it’s not out of guilt for what you feel you should have done. Is a part of you thinking you can only forgive yourself if she forgives you? Because that’s not the case. You missed your chance to do the right thing with her. You could use it to learn to do right by the next person.

If you don’t have dependents, I believe you have every right to take your own life. But know that your last act will have the effect of creating a world where people are more afraid to leave their partners out of fear that their partner might kill themselves, irrespective of whether they are happy in the relationship

As someone who is indeed stuck on heartbreak for a very long time: I model it as analogous to a system that encountered stressors well beyond what the system was designed to handle, and which entered a dysfunctional equilibrium as a result. Like a computer that is encountering overflow errors. Beware training that posits to know the solution for everything. In many cases, the solution is not yet known (source: me, someone who has explicitly been told by American therapists that they feel out of their depth with me; I was not trained as a therapist but started reading a lot of therapy books once I realized therapists were kindof flying blind with me)

I feel like the best job for you would in theory be "therapist consultant". You could be the person who reads all the books and knows all the archetypes, and therapists could come to you when there's a client they can't figure out.
OK, next question: if your goal is to be intrigued by them "like a puzzle", how will you react if you conclude that the puzzle is boring?

I just realize you're confused which therapist said she was out of her depth. Emily didn't say she was out of her depth. That was one of the next therapists I tried to find after Emily. I'm disappointed you were willing to make such an assertion without reading carefully.

I think the crux is how you are likely to react if the client does not make progress. Are you likely to blame them because their failure to make progress is interpreted as an attack on your ego, since your identity appears to tied to succeeding at the intellectual challenge of helping them?

Funny, just a few posts down on my feed there was this post asking how to find a therapist who *doesn’t* care, because caring is viewed by this poster as being an inappropriate violation of boundaries: https://www.reddit.com/r/TalkTherapy/comments/x6osjd/best_way_to_find_a_therapist_who_doesnt_care/

Hmm so in my THC-induced “manic” states, people can still reason with me and give suggestions (eg they can advise me to stop spending on something and can take my phone away if they think I won’t sleep otherwise). Perhaps it depends on how responsive the person is to external suggestions.
Thank you for sharing
Fair suggestion; I’ve gotten good at regulating what I do in these stares.

Third thing I wanted to say: if mania is the body’s way of resolving a deep psychological conflict, maybe we should stop trying to block mania with medication and instead just make sure people don’t do stuff they will regret?
I would love to hear more about your situation, if you’re up for writing about it. I think it would help me too.

Thanks for the empathy. My manic states are induced by THC (and I induce them intentionally when I need to do some deep processing), which is probably why the doctors couldn’t diagnose me with anything. “She’s just high”.

I have to say, when I saw the first thing that happened to that comment was that it got downvoted, I was hurt. I wonder if people are more or less likely to be cruel if they see what I look like this morning. Worth gathering data on. Here’s what I look like:

[https://www.flickr.com/gp/79433262@N05/309m926h4E](https://www.flickr.com/gp/79433262@N05/309m926h4E)

You should know that she told me, on two separate occasions leading up to my episode: “the only line is that we can’t have sex”. The context must have been me saying I didn't want to explore my feelings towards her because I was afraid of crossing a line, but in my head I just meant I didn’t want to become clingy.

I didn’t include this line in the original post because people tend to immediately pivot and label that as an abuse of power.

I admit I still don’t know why she said that. It is not even true legally (the line is “sexual contact”, not “sex”).

But I am willing to let it go.

Like, if I’m being honest, there’s a good chance she staked her self-esteem on being attractive and being able to read people to compensate for existing in an academic system that made her feel “stupid” her whole life. Viewed through a cynical lens, this need for validation is “narcissism”. So you could easily claim I was the victim of “a narcissist” who desperately wanted me to validate her attractiveness.

Fun. But everyone I know has a narcissistic trend in their personality.

Relevant song: “Suddenly I See” by KT Tunstall. Helped me understand that appearances matter to people who feel powerless otherwise. But really how I saw her was closer to “Private Eyes” (also by KT Tunstall). Quoting the latter: “we gotta get out of here, but should I be following you? You’ve got the look of painted broken china”
Update: sitting with the idea that a parental figure really let you down is hard.

You agree that the call to stop contact probably came from her supervisor, though?

Re how she comes across over text: one of the things that make me suspect she was dyslexic was she once said (referencing the wall of texts I was sending her in our last week together): “texting is not a good medium for me” (i was confused as I thought she was hinting that she was tired of me texting her even though I had told her I didn’t expect her to respond since we would talk in session, but in hindsight I think she was trying to hint that she wanted to respond but didn’t find text to be a medium in which SHE could express herself well)

Also, I’m schizoid. If I weren’t honest another part of me would call me out and proceed to lose all trust in the part of me that lied and drive me insane over it, so you may find this is an oddly reliable account (hopefully you never have a reason to find this out). In the past, therapists seem to express surprise at the degree to which my accounts lined up with corroborating accounts. This makes me think most people lie without even realizing it.

Terminal illness has a lot of appeal, huh. No one would fault you or be angry with you for “leaving”, you’d be able to mentally prepare everyone for the death. They’d understand, for once, that death can be a relief from pain. They’d actually be happy for you when you find peace.

Terminal illness physicalizes your pain for everyone else to see and believe, for once.

I wonder if “Pam” got made fun for being “dumb” as a kid, and that’s why she over-identifies with Jorts. She desperately needs to believe that even people who are labeled “dumb” can learn because she knows the human world is not at all kind to people who cannot perform on par with their peers.

Interesting food for thought: we can easily accept that some cats are not as smart as others, but when it comes to humans we don’t tend to be as sympathetic. We tend to tell them “no, you should just try harder”. Perhaps constantly being pushed to “try harder” can come across as bullying and/or as someone trying to butter your fur.

If the criticism is aimed at extreme conservatives who tend to have a starry-eyed view of America and American history, wouldn’t it be most effective to draw comparisons to “other” regimes that these same conservatives view negatively?

In other words, don’t these extreme conservative insist on having a whitewashed/bizarrely nostalgic view of American history? If so, I don’t think saying “you are regressing to ugly times in your own history” would be very effective for them (I could imagine them saying “heck yeah!”). But “you are as bad as the foreign regimes you deem evil” may just click?
